    n = len(customers_list)

    def route_cost(route):

            # tie-breaker to be deterministic

    # Maintain route endpoints for fast check

        return (r[0], r[-1])

        rj = route_of.get(j, None)

            continue
        route_i = routes[ri]
        route_j = routes[rj]
        # Check if i and j are at compatible ends for merge
        li, ri_end = endpoints(route_i)
        lj, rj_end = endpoints(route_j)

        # Possible merges:
        # - route_i ends with i and route_j starts with j => route_i + route_j
        # - route_j ends with j and route_i starts with i => route_j + route_i
        # - Additionally handle reversed concatenation when i is at start, etc.

            tot = 0
            for x in route:
                tot += demands[x]
            return tot

            merged = route_i + route_j

        elif ri_end == i and rj_end == j:
            merged = route_i + route_j[::-1]

        # But we stored route_of mapping by index, so we must update indices carefully.

        keep = ri
        drop = rj

            continue

        # To avoid complex index updates, rebuild route_of for all routes after removal.
        routes.pop(drop)
        route_of = {}
        for idx, r in enumerate(routes):

                route_of[x] = idx

            # Early stop: keep merges tight but still allow further improvement

            # Continue a few more merges if savings are strongly positive

    # Deterministically try to absorb shortest routes into others when capacity allows

        tot = 0

        if removed:
